### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 82 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e7b32dedf15cbda1815aacc8c293620e2cae86e1` — the merge of head `d4414410c797989ecdf4983e7633b32df94619d3` into base `272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e7b32dedf15cbda1815aacc8c293620e2cae86e1 && git checkout e7b32dedf15cbda1815aacc8c293620e2cae86e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41 d4414410c797989ecdf4983e7633b32df94619d3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41 && git merge --no-ff d4414410c797989ecdf4983e7633b32df94619d3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 272fec05bdf48e8dd06f2be252ef4aeb67740f41` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f82fd682510fca9bd7ab9727ba50ae299558048b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/field-patch-targets.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts (`scalarOverridesPackagedBase`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extender-fold.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, docs/adr/0146 D10, docs/adr/0029 D9.2a, content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx, .changeset/28565-field-patch-applied.md

Inputs read: card #28565 body and its three comments (unblock record, claim 6558511726, dev report 6560090896), PR #28728 body, its one bot comment, the 18-file net diff against `main` (merge-base `d62d9737`), and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff outside the `hits` file is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; it is read here only to judge the schema file against its first consumers.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `ObjectExtensionSchema` (the hits file): unchanged.** The diff moves only prose in `object.zod.ts`: the `fieldPatches` `.describe()` loses `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` and the N-23d forward reference, the TSDoc, the `@example` comment and the guidance code comment follow. `FieldDisplayPatchSchema`, `whitelistedPatchShape`, `refuseExtensionFieldPatchKeys` and the `.strict()` key set are untouched; nothing an author can write is added, refused or re-typed by the schema itself. Right.
- **Liveness verdict of `data/ObjectExtension:fieldPatches` flips experimental to live.** The liveness ledger resolves `experimental` from exactly this marker (`packages/spec/liveness/README.md:77`), no `packages/spec/liveness/*.json` row names `objectExtensions` or `fieldPatches` (grep: none), `authorable-surface/data.json:691` lists the key without a marker, and the `Spec property liveness` check-run on the head is green. The spec test that pinned the marker now pins its absence and the sentence naming `mergeObjectDefinitions`. Right: the consumer the marker waited for is in the same diff.
- **The sentence the description now publishes is true in the tree, clause by clause**, checked against the cited code rather than the PR body:
  - "Applied by the registry merge (`mergeObjectDefinitions`) after the additive merges, on every object read": `engine.ts:8993-9008` carries `fieldPatches` onto `extDef` at the one `'extend'` registration (git grep on the head: one call site); `registry.ts#mergeObjectDefinitions` applies `applyFieldPatches` after the `fields` spread, the by-name rule merge, the index concat and the three scalar overrides; the fold `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` is the one implementation behind `resolveObject` (list read), `resolveOwnerLayer` (code layer) and `foldObjectExtendersOnto` (the by-name read in `protocol-object-extender-fold.ts:60-62`, unedited and correctly so). Right.
  - "a tenant's own text keeps winning": `tenantPatchedDisplayKeys` is computed once over the fold's base, compares the `own` contributor's field and option against the base's through `scalarOverridesPackagedBase` (the D9.2a predicate, imported, with the same two "no opinion" edges as `tenantAuthoredScalars`: no owner, base IS the owner by reference). Right, and faithful to ADR-0029 D9.2a's binding consequences (computed once over the base, never against the folded owner layer, no flag stamped).
  - "between two extensions the higher `priority` wins": contributors fold in ascending priority, the yield set does not move with the running merge, so the later (higher) write stands. Right; pinned by the registry test's "whichever registers first" case.
  - "A patch naming a field or option value the target does not have is refused at install and by `os validate`": install-local step 2e refuses `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with every refusal in `details.refusals` before any write (sits after the 2d override gate, before the hot-register); `validate.ts` step 3a-iv exits 1 with each refusal located. Both ask `@objectstack/metadata-core`'s `fieldPatchTargetRefusals`, and the registry's boot warning asks `fieldPatchTargetMisses`, so the three cannot disagree on the verdict given the same target. Right. The brief's "both install doors" is honestly reduced to one: `protocol-package-install.ts:230` parses with `PackageInstallManifestSchema` = `ManifestSchema.extend(...)`, and `ManifestSchema` is a `strictObject` with no `objectExtensions` key (`kernel/manifest.zod.ts:485`), so no extension can reach that door; verified in the live tree, not taken from the PR body.
- **Public surface:** `@objectstack/metadata-core` gains three exports (`fieldPatchTargetMisses`, `fieldPatchTargetRefusals`, `fieldPatchTargetRefusalMessage`) and a type pair; `mergeObjectDefinitions` (module-private) gains a fifth positional parameter and its one caller passes it; `ObjectExtensionParsed` and `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST` are consumed from `@objectstack/spec/data`, both already exported on `main`. Keys applied are read from the constant, so the whitelist stays the one list (ADR-0146 D10: "the whitelist the write gate reads, never a judgement the gate makes"). Right.
- **Picklist-bound fields:** the fold skips `options` on a field with a non-empty `picklist` (the served options are the list's, written by `finishServedObject` after the fold), and the judge refuses such an option patch as `picklist-option` at both doors and in the boot log. The three agree, and the choice is the honest one: a label written in the fold would never be served. Right; the docs page says so in one sentence.
- **Idempotence of `foldObjectExtendersOnto` over a folded body:** a base already carrying "Sector" reads as authored against the owner's "Industry", so the patch yields and the value stays — the same mechanism ADR-0029 D9.2a records for the scalars, and the same recorded cost: a tenant overlay written back verbatim from a served body freezes the extension's current patch text, and a package upgrade that changes the patch text does not reach that tenant. That edge is ruled and written into the ADR ("recorded here rather than papered over"); the card asked for exactly the scalars' yield. Right, not a finding.
- **Uninstall restores the vendor's text:** the registered owner declaration is never mutated (`applyFieldPatches` copies on write, returns by reference when nothing applies), the fold recomputes from contributors, and the cache drops with the contributor. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `28565-field-patch-applied.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec` — the five packages the diff moves, no package moved is missing, no package listed is unmoved (`metadata-protocol` is read, not edited, and is rightly absent). `Metadata-protocol: semantic` takes at least `minor` on each moved package (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). Level: right.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the card's own ruling (item 5: "a declared key gains its effect"). Read against the AGENTS precedence rule it could also be spelled `narrowed` (a value the install door admitted is now refused; "several ⇒ narrowed over semantic") — but the value it refuses was declared not enforced, the level is identical either way, and the card fixed the kind. Accepted as ruled; recorded, not a finding.
- `Clause-②: no`, no arm, in both carriers: no published accept set is widened, and the refusal lands on a slot whose `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` marker was the published promise, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. The three new `metadata-core` exports are a public-surface addition that the line's own question (「扩大公开面吗」) could read as `yes (widening)`; the seat's claim set `no`, and at this tier nothing turns on it. Recorded, not a finding.
- `check:adr-0087-registration` is not owed (no breaking arm). `Check Changeset` on the head: green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `deviations` (6560090896), each answered:
1. **`installPackage` call line not written** — verified in the live tree (`PackageInstallManifestSchema` extends a strict `ManifestSchema` with no `objectExtensions` key): a call there could never fire. Accepted; the card's "both install doors" reduces to install-local, and the record above says so.
2. **`validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` edited outside the file surface** — the closed roster requires the new validate-only gate to be classified; the row names the build-side gap honestly. Accepted.
3. **`ObjectExtensionSchema.guidance.actions` left unchanged "under ruling 3"** — no ruling 3 exists in the card's comments (three comments: unblock, claim, report); the claim's file surface names "the N-23a slot's EXPERIMENTAL marker" only. The sentence is in the `hits` file and is now false by one key. Escalated as should-fix S2 below.
4. **`protocol-object-extender-fold.ts` needed no edit** — verified (`:60-62` calls `registry.foldObjectExtendersOnto`, the one apply path). Accepted.

`open_questions`: none declared. `out_of_scope_findings`: (b) `os build` runs no target check — recorded in `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` with its reason, outside the card's three doors, accepted as reported; (c) the skills doc names `fields`/`priority` only — `Skills-docs: follow-up #28730` on the PR body. No PR comment raises anything (the one comment is the docs-drift advisory, which flags `metadata-core/src/index.ts` as un-anchored; the page that documents the new exports is `object-extensions.mdx`, which the diff updates).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** — judged against ADR-0146 D10 (second rule) and its first consumer, `registry.ts#mergeObjectDefinitions`, with the install door and `os validate` as the refusal's readers.

The design holds. ADR-0146 D10 asks for exactly three things and the tree does each: the patch is a per-field map in the extension body (the slot N-23a declared, carried byte-for-byte as `ObjectExtensionParsed['fieldPatches']`, no second shape anywhere — `git grep fieldPatches` on the head finds no other reader), `mergeObjectDefinitions` applies it after the additive merges, and the ADR-0029 D9.2a scalar yield applies to it through the one imported predicate. The description now published is a true account of the tree (① above), the marker flip is consistent with every consumer of the marker (liveness ledger, authorable surface, lint's experimental hint, the generated reference page, the spec test), and the boot path never refuses (AGENTS.md *Startup registry reads*): `reportFieldPatchMisses` warns once per object/package/field/option and the next fold applies a patch whose target has since arrived.

Attempts to break it, and what each found:

- *Tenant edit vs extension patch, including a re-fold of a folded body and a package upgrade changing the patch text* — consistent with D9.2a in every case, including its recorded "verbatim write-back freezes the extender's text" edge. No finding.
- *Two extensions on one key* — higher priority wins by write order over a yield set that does not move. No finding.
- *Picklist-bound fields* — fold, install door, validate and boot log all answer "not patchable here". No finding.
- *Does the install-door judge and the validate judge agree with what the fold applies?* — **Not on a field another extension adds.** The fold applies a patch to `merged.fields` as it stands when that extender's turn comes, so a patch on a field added by a *lower*-priority extender applies and one on a field added by a *higher*-priority extender is skipped and warned on every read (the docblock's "applies on the next read once the field arrives" is only true for the owner arriving later, not for this order). The install door judges against the registry's fully resolved object (every installed extender's field present, in any priority), so it admits such a patch. `os validate` judges against the composed stack's declared `objects` only (`cli/src/utils/field-patch-targets.ts#declaredObjects`), so it refuses the same patch when the adding extension is in the same stack. The same split applies to a patch on a field the *same* extension adds through `fields`: fold applies, both doors refuse. The published description says "the target object's own fields" (the conservative reading, under which validate is right and the other two are lenient), while `registry.ts` and `object-extensions.mdx` claim "reaches a field a lower-priority extender added". Three readers, two answers, on a case outside the sentence the spec publishes. **Should-fix S1** — pick one: judge all three against the owner's own fields (drop the "lower-priority extender" claim from the registry docblock and the docs page, and have the install door read the owner layer), or apply patches in a second pass after every extender has merged and let `declaredObjects` compose extension-added fields. Not a must-fix: the spec's own sentence is kept true, validate green still implies install admits (validate is the strict one), and the card's tests all run on the owner's fields.
- *Fields in array vs record spelling across the three readers* — the judge reads both spellings; the fold's `recordFieldOf` reads the record spelling only (the registry's merge contract: `fields` is spread). A body handed to `foldObjectExtendersOnto` with array-spelled fields is neither patched nor warned, because the warning is derived from the judge, which finds the field. Registry-registered bodies are records, so this is an edge of the public fold entry, not of a shipped read. **Should-fix S3**, small: have the fold warn by its own reader, or normalise once.
- *Removing the marker: every consumer* — consistent (① above). The one stale sentence is in the hits file itself: `guidance.actions` still says "the merge carries `fields`, `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, `validations` and `indexes` only", while the code comment four lines above now lists `fieldPatches`. A refusal prescription an author is shown, now one key short. **Should-fix S2**, one-line edit; it is a sentence about `actions`, so nothing it refuses is wrong.
- *Changeset levels and declaration lines* — ② above; no finding.

Findings:
- Must-fix: none.
- Should-fix S1: the three readers disagree on a patch naming a field an extension adds (fold: priority-order dependent; install door: admitted; `os validate`: refused); settle one answer and align `registry.ts`'s docblock and `object-extensions.mdx`'s "lower-priority extension" claim with the spec's "own fields".
- Should-fix S2: `ObjectExtensionSchema.guidance.actions` in `object.zod.ts` lists six carried keys "only"; add `fieldPatches`.
- Should-fix S3: the fold's miss report is derived from a judge that reads array-spelled fields while the fold itself patches record-spelled fields only; an array-spelled body through `foldObjectExtendersOnto` is silently unpatched.

Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: no failure, no cancellation; the lint, spec-liveness, changeset, queue-guard, docs and type-check source gates are green; the core and UI test shards, workspace type-check and E2E lanes were still in progress. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts and govern over this prose when they land.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d4414410c797989ecdf4983e7633b32df94619d3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-field-patch-targets.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save door's `VALIDATION_ERROR` envelope), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`)

This record is a DELTA of the earlier record on this PR (comment 6560336731, head `f82fd682`): everything that record judged and does not name here stands unchanged, its three should-fix findings (S1 fold/install/validate disagreement on an extension-added field, S2 the stale `guidance.actions` sentence, S3 the record-only fold reader) included — none of them is addressed in the delta. Read: the net diff against `main` at this head (18 files, merge-base `db357f6d`), the delta `f82fd682..d4414410` restricted to the PR's files, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing posted.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The hits file is unchanged.** `git diff f82fd682 d4414410 -- packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` is empty, and the net hunk against the new merge-base is byte-identical (same digest, `index` lines excluded) to the one judged at `f82fd682`. The earlier ① judgments on the accept set, the liveness flip and the published sentence hold as written; `Spec property liveness` is green on this head too.
- **Every other net hunk of this PR is byte-identical to the earlier head** for `registry.ts`, `metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts`, `metadata-core/src/index.ts`, `cli/src/utils/field-patch-targets.ts`, `object-extensions.mdx`, the changeset and the spec test (digest-compared per file). `engine.ts`'s net hunk is the same five-line `fieldPatches: ext.fieldPatches` carry; the other `engine.ts` lines in the delta (`isUnparseableDate`, `UNPARSEABLE_DATE_FAULT`) are `main`'s own and are not in the net diff. Right.
- **The merge kept both ADR-0146 D10 features intact at all three readers**, judged on the tree:
  - `os validate`: #28724's `__c` reservation is step 3a-iv (`findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals`, its own exit-1 branch) and this PR's target check is step 3a-v right after it, the block whole (judge call, JSON branch, `printError`, bullet list, exit 1) and 3b following. Neither step shadows the other. Right.
  - the install door: #28724's judge sits at 1c'' (before the manifest service, on both branches, `judgeExtensionFieldSuffix` per delivered package) and this PR's 2e sits after the 2d override gate and before the hot-register, unchanged. Both imports resolve from their packages (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` for the suffix judge, `@objectstack/metadata-core` for the target judge). Right.
  - the registry fold: `registry.ts` is untouched by the merge; `engine.ts` carries the slot as before. Right.
- **`VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` holds both rows** (`findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals` from #28724, `findFieldPatchTargetRefusals` from this PR), each with its reason, and the ledger's docblock was reworded to say it holds two. The closed roster is satisfied by the tree, not by a merge marker. Right.
- **`d4414410c`** gives the two field-patch validate spawn tests a `120_000` budget; the sibling spawn file `validate-extension-field-suffix.test.ts` on `main` carries the same figure on each of its cases. Test-only, no accept-set or surface change. Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the earlier record: `minor` on the five moved packages, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` as the card ruled, `Clause-②: no` with no arm.
